_comment: Profile-banner formats and the parts of them a platform covers or crops, as design guides state
them. These are facts about a platform, not about an app, which is why they live in the engine: an
app's banner config names one by key. Lengths are pixels of the canvas the platform asks for.
`zones` are what the rules judge: a `keep-out` box is covered (the profile photo), a `keep-in` box
is what survives the narrowest crop. `photos` are the round profile photo as the guides preview
draws it, centre and diameter. Where sources disagree the most cautious figure is taken and the
others are named. A new platform gets an entry here, with the URLs and the date read.

_source: LinkedIn Help publishes no pixel figures for the personal cover image: https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a7145577 (read 2026-10-19)
_note: Canvas 1584 x 396 (4:1) in every source; JPG or PNG, 8 MB. Desktop: the round photo sits bottom-left,
about 210 px across at banner scale, 30-40 px from the left edge, its upper half over the banner;
guides give the covered area as 152-568 px wide, so the keep-out is widened to x < 450, y > 180.
Mobile: the sides are cropped by 60 px (ScreenSnap) to 317 px (contentin.io, centre 60 % visible),
and about 44 px top and bottom (Zeliq, 22 % of the height); the narrowest is the keep-in. Where the
photo sits on mobile the sources disagree (bottom-left and larger: contentin.io, MagicStudio; bottom
centre: Zeliq, SocialRails, RightBlogger), so both are kept out.
